items.component: Egress control of bridge-network container steps
items.mitigation: Bridge-network steps (fetch, TUF refresh, positives) restrict names (dead DNS plus a per-step --add-host allowlist), not raw IP connections. Only --network none steps prove zero egress (N-MISSING, T-NONET, admission negatives). All code that runs in these containers is hash-pinned (R-30).

items.component: Docker daemon, kernel and host as trusted computing base; build and capture containers not --read-only
items.version: daemon and kernel as recorded by init
items.mitigation: The daemon, kernel and host are trusted (the host fs.protected_hardlinks value is UNKNOWN). Build and capture containers are not --read-only because dpkg must write the root filesystem; they are ephemeral --rm containers with --cap-drop ALL plus the minimum caps and no-new-privileges, and install only hash-pinned .debs. Verifier containers run --read-only with a private tmpfs /tmp.

items.component: Image identity as reported by the Docker image store
items.version: classic or containerd store, recorded by init
items.mitigation: init records the image-store and driver type. Identity accepts Id == pinned config digest (classic store) or Id == pinned index digest (containerd store), nothing else, plus RepoDigests containing the pinned index digest and RootFS.Layers == the pinned diffIds (AC-02, S5). The metadata reported by the daemon is trusted (R-03). The hosted CI image 20261004.327.1 ships Docker 28.0.4; the local D14 store type is UNKNOWN until init records it.

items.component: cryptography 50.0.2 with statically linked OpenSSL 4.0.3 (a second OpenSSL in the verifier process)
items.mitigation: 0 of 43 OpenSSL 4.0 advisories affect 4.0.3 (every 4.0 range ends before 4.0.3). The static copy exports no OpenSSL symbols (ELF check on cryptography/hazmat/bindings/_rust.abi3.so), so it cannot shadow the system libcrypto.so.3 that W binds, and exactly one libcrypto.so.3 is mapped (S4). The basename _rust.abi3.so is shared with W, so it is not used as a probe prefix.

items.component: sigstore-python RFC 3161 signed-timestamp handling
items.mitigation: By design sigstore verify identity accepts a bundle whose signed timestamp fails to verify while the transparency-log integrated time verifies (verifier.py:146-150). CHAR-TSA (AC-12) records this as a characterization only; it is never counted or described as a rejection. tsa-direct (AC-11) exercises the rfc3161-client library API separately.

items.component: zlib (libz.so.1, mapped through zlib, binascii and libcrypto.so.3)
items.mitigation: Loaded (libz.so.1 through zlib, binascii and libcrypto.so.3); not reachable. CVE-2026-27171 (no-dsa minor, CPU loop in x2nmodp): its entry points crc32_combine, crc32_combine64, crc32_combine_gen and crc32_combine_gen64 are defined only by libz.so.1.3.1 and imported by none of the 753 ELF objects in the four image layers and the 31 wheels; inside libz only the two wrappers reach them (objdump). CVE-2026-85091 (untriaged, gz_vacate overflow through non-blocking gzwrite/gzprintf, stated for 1.3.1.2 through 1.3.2 while the image has 1.3.1): the gz* entry points are imported only by usr/bin/dpkg-deb and libapt-pkg.so.7.0.0, both outside the verifier process closure; mapping dpkg-deb is S4 (not in runtime.files) and mapping libapt-pkg is S3 (runtime.blockedObjects). The version-range reading is recorded, not relied on. No fix in trixie; residual, accepted only through ownerAcceptance. No waiver.

items.component: XZ Utils liblzma (liblzma.so.5 through _lzma)
items.mitigation: Present, not loaded. The fix (5.8.1-1+deb13u2 in trixie-security, DSA-6549-1, .deb SHA256 b38acab3...84ec) is not applied because it would change the admitted image identity. _lzma is statically reachable (sigstore._cli -> sigstore.oidc -> webbrowser -> shutil -> lzma; requests.utils -> zipfile -> lzma), so non-loading depends on the S3 guard (lzma and _lzma blocked; shutil and zipfile handle the ImportError) in every verifier process, including venv creation. Any mapping STOPs with S1 (and with S3 through blockedObjects).

items.component: GNU C Library: 6 open records with HIGH or CRITICAL scores, not reachable
items.mitigation: OWNER REVIEW FLAGGED (research ownerReview true). No newer glibc in trixie, trixie-updates or trixie-security (S1 not triggered). CVE-2019-1010022 (NVD 9.8) is a mitigation bypass without a standalone defect; CVE-2018-20796 and CVE-2019-9192 need attacker regex patterns and no verifier ELF imports glibc regex; CVE-2019-1010023 needs ldd on an attacker ELF, which the verifier never runs; CVE-2026-19499 (strfmon) and CVE-2026-5435 (libresolv debug printers) have no importer in the verifier closure (static .dynsym scan, cross-checked by the main session). Not reachable, so S2 does not apply; the import closure is pinned by S4 and S5.

items.component: GNU C Library DNS stub resolver initialization with a long search list
items.mitigation: Conditional: the verifier resolves names through glibc (getaddrinfo is imported by _socket and by the cryptography _rust.abi3.so), and a search or domain entry of about 200 or more characters in /etc/resolv.conf or LOCALDOMAIN aborts the process (availability only; verification fails closed). Guard S7: containers run --dns 127.0.0.1 --dns-search . and probe-runtime records /etc/resolv.conf and STOPs unless nameserver is exactly 127.0.0.1, no search or domain entry exists and LOCALDOMAIN, RES_OPTIONS and HOSTALIASES are unset. Fixed upstream in 2.45; Debian no-dsa for trixie.

items.component: GNU C Library: 12 open MEDIUM or LOW records, not reachable
items.mitigation: No newer glibc in trixie (S1 not triggered). Per the research: glob, wordexp, tdelete, the libresolv debug printers and the iconv JISX0213 converters have no importer in the verifier closure; no component passes an untrusted ',ccs=' fopen mode; CVE-2019-1010024 and CVE-2019-1010025 are ASLR mitigation bypasses without a standalone defect; CVE-2026-86805 and CVE-2026-95818 need setuid programs and a local attacker, both absent from the container. items.component: CPython stdlib tempfile.TemporaryDirectory cleanup race
items.mitigation: Affects the image: the [3.12] backport was reverted before the tag and the image tempfile.py lacks the fix (the CNA range is wrong). tempfile is imported eagerly, but the only TemporaryDirectory() call on the eager import path of the verifier is importlib.resources._common.as_file, which sigstore does not use, and exploitation needs a local attacker modifying the temporary tree during cleanup. Verifier containers use a private tmpfs /tmp.

items.component: CPython stdlib base64 and binascii decoding (altchars; stop at the first padded quad)
items.mitigation: Affects the image (no [3.12] backport; fixed only on newer branches). base64 is imported eagerly and decodes bundle fields, so the lenient decoding is reachable from bundle input. The decoded values are inputs to signature, certificate, transparency-log and digest checks, which N-CORRUPT, L-SET and MAL-TSA exercise; exploitability was not analyzed beyond the static call-site review in the research. MEDIUM, so S2 does not apply.

items.mitigation: Affects the image; http.cookies is imported eagerly through requests.compat, but js_output() is never called by the frozen wheels (only inside http.cookies itself).

items.mitigation: Affects the image; imaplib and poplib are not imported by sigstore verification (eager closure or upper bound).

items.mitigation: The CNA range includes 3.12.15, but the defect (a user-writable default mime.types path) is Windows-only; mimetypes is imported (urllib3.fields), and the condition does not exist on the Linux image.

items.component: cffi _cffi_backend with statically linked libffi (3.4.6 inferred)
items.mitigation: libffi is statically linked (no cffi.libs/). Version 3.4.6 is inferred from the cffi CI configuration at the v2.1.0 tag plus binary markers, not from authenticated provenance (PyPI provenance HTTP 404). No CVE affects 3.4.6, but later upstream hardening (3.5.2, 3.7.0) is absent. _cffi_backend is not statically reachable from the verifier; the wheel is admitted by hash pin (R-30).

items.component: 30 unchanged D13 PyPI wheels (also installer, sdist, official rfc3161 wheel and 5 tool wheels) trusted by hash pins only
items.mitigation: Every wheel equals its PyPI sha256 for the exact filename and none is yanked; admission (exactly one wheel per pin, size and sha256, inert ZIP and RECORD checks) runs before any import, and installs use --validate-record all without index access. No PyPI provenance or attestation is verified (cffi has none; the sdist gitTag and gitCommit come from an unverified attestation), so trust rests on the PyPI-served bytes at capture time and on the release process of each project. 36 of 37 packages have no known advisory; pytest 9.0.2 is remediated (R-09).

items.component: Rust crate chacha20 compiled into W (through rand 0.10.2)
items.mitigation: Yanked on crates.io (reason not stated) but compiled from the unchanged official Cargo.lock; no RustSec or GHSA advisory for 0.10.x. The only documented later fix (0.10.2 changelog) is a correctness fix for an SSE4.1 intrinsic in the SSE2 backend. The lock is not modified (no patch policy).

items.component: Rust crate anyhow in Cargo.lock, not compiled for the target
items.mitigation: Informational (unsound) advisory for Error::downcast_mut(). anyhow is reached only through wasm-only crates (wit-bindgen*, wasm-metadata, wit-component, wit-parser), so it is not compiled into W for x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu; the all-target cargo fetch (B3) downloads and checksum-verifies its .crate but nothing builds it. The official Cargo.lock is not modified.

items.component: Rust code outside advisory-database coverage and without declared MSRV: rfc3161-client and tsp-asn1 (local), cryptography-x509 0.50.1 (git), and the local crates inside cryptography 50.0.2
items.mitigation: These crates parse bundle timestamp data or certificates, but no advisory database covers them. rfc3161-client and tsp-asn1 declare no rust_version (10 compiled crates declare none; the highest declared is 1.85 against rustc 1.85.1); an MSRV failure fails the build closed (STOP), it cannot weaken it. The git checkout must equal ffde75a2 (prepare).

items.component: Rust crate openssl-src (vendored OpenSSL 3.6.2 C sources)
items.mitigation: Compiled as an optional build dependency of openssl-sys, but with OPENSSL_NO_VENDOR=1 its C sources are not built and W links the system libcrypto.so.3; the ELF gate (wheel-audit) proves this later: NEEDED subset, PKCS7_verify undefined at OPENSSL_3.0.0, zero defined OpenSSL symbols, no 'OpenSSL 3.6' bytes (also an S3 condition). 41 of 61 OpenSSL 3.6 advisories affect 3.6.2, including HIGH CVE-2026-84782 and CVE-2026-45447 (PKCS7_verify use-after-free), which is why the official vendored wheel is rejected (AC-05). Whether a newer openssl-src fixes all of them was not researched; the official Cargo.lock is not modified.

items.component: Debian trixie build closure for W (about 82 packages incl. rustc and cargo 1.85.1, maturin 1.8.3, gcc 14, binutils 2.44, python3.13, libexpat1, libllvm19, curl, gnutls, krb5 and ldap stacks, libgit2, libssh2)
items.version: gcc=4:14.2.0-1, binutils=2.44-3, rustc and cargo 1.85.1+dfsg1-1+deb13u1, python3-maturin 1.8.3-1, libc6-dev 2.41-12+deb13u4, libssl-dev 3.5.7-1~deb13u3
items.mitigation: Build-only: installed from hash-pinned .debs into fresh build containers that run --network none on hash-pinned inputs (sdist, Cargo.lock-checksummed crates), and W is reproduced (B1 == B2 == W, CI B1 == W). Open tracker records in the closure include binutils (69), curl (25) and expat 2.8.3 (7, incl. CVE-2026-77214 HIGH); none of these sources has a newer fixed version, and no closure package is loaded by the verifier. maturin --compatibility linux makes --auditwheel check a no-op (audit.rs:297, :484), so the ELF gate (wheel-audit) is the real linkage control. The closure was modelled from the Packages index (apt not run); the signed apt capture in D14 is the authority.

items.component: Docker Official Image python:3.12.15-slim-trixie build provenance
items.mitigation: Identity is pinned by digest (index, manifest, config, diffIds; S5) and the frozen layers were re-hashed, but the in-toto/SPDX attestations of the image were only matched by subject digest: no signature, issuer, TUF or transparency check was run (cryptographicallyAuthenticated false). Trust rests on the digest-addressed bytes served by Docker Hub and on the Official Images build process.

items.component: Evidence mount /out writable by every container, including verifier subprocesses
items.mitigation: Bounded: code execution inside a verifier container already defeats the outputs of that container, and all code executed there is hash-pinned (image digest, 31 wheels, W, installer, d09.py bound by the receipt). The fresh replay of the gate (--replay) recomputes every outcome, so evidence from an earlier run cannot be reused. The S4 admitted set (manifest-a and manifest-b) is written under /out; passing its sha256 between steps or mounting it read-only is a recommended hardening.
